name: Geba
overview: Geba, also known as Gaba, is a city within the tribe of Benjamin that was assigned to the sons of Aaron, highlighting its Levitical significance (Joshua 21:17). The city is mentioned as a dwelling place for Benjamin's descendants and as a strategic location during times of conflict, as seen when enemies lodged there causing fear in nearby Ramah and Gibeah (Nehemiah 11:31; Isaiah 10:29). Additionally, Geba is referenced in connection with the surrounding villages built by the singers near Jerusalem and is part of the plain stretching from Geba to Rimmon, indicating its geographical and communal importance in biblical times (Nehemiah 12:29; Zechariah 14:10).
